description: ABI Coverage Grid manifest — the single source of truth for thin-corner runtime coverage cells. See src/docs/Design/abi-coverage-grid.md. Phase 1 enumerates the closure / inout / tuple corners as a full cross-product and grades each cell on every declared+exercised runtime (sim = Mono JIT, device = NativeAOT). Cells map to tests by (class, method) name over the existing test-results JSONL + TestClasses.g.txt inventory; rename-rot (a cite absent from the inventory) is a hard integrity error. Disposition: expect-green (release-gating), supported-low-priority (reported, not gated), by-design-gray (intentionally unsupported, cites a roadmap rationale). DOCUMENTED ABSENCES (deliberately out of slice-1 scope, recorded here per design §5 rather than silently dropped): nested tuple returns ((A,B),C) — no fixture authored; sync tuple returns with a generic element (only the async-on-generic-parent shape exists, and it is suppressed by design — see tuple.ret.pair.contains-generic.async); async-closure-PARAM fan-out (the closure-PARAM and closure-RETURN fan-out legs are both authored here as closure.fanout.same-signature.closure-param / closure.fanout.same-signature.closure-return; the async leg shares the same emitter gap and is deferred to the decision point after the sync legs' fix lands); non-void closure RETURN (the closure-returning materialiser — IsDispatchableClosureReturningMethod — dispatches only a zero-arg `() -> Void` returned closure; a non-void returned closure like `() -> Int32` falls to the fatalError stub and is an unimplemented capability, orthogonal to the fan-out Latent, so the closure-RETURN fan-out cells use the supported `() -> Void` shape with a C#-side side-effect oracle); the full closure direction×escaping×effects×arity cross-product (the basics are already covered by existing ClosureTests/ClosureEdgeCaseTests and represented below; only the Latent-tied fan-out leg is newly authored).

cells.runtimeNote: Roadmap Latent 'Same-signature closure/async method fan-out gap' — the closure-PARAM leg the plain/async sibling fan-out fix did not reach. Rare in consumer code (no validation-set library produces it), so dispositioned supported-low-priority: a red is reported in the grid (the grid's purpose is to REACH this Latent), not release-gating. Reached on sim+device.
Control: the same shared closure-param method dispatched through the OWNER existential reads its own populated vtable, so it must be green independent of the fan-out fix.

Roadmap Latent 'Same-signature closure/async method fan-out gap' — the closure-RETURN leg. Twin of the closure-param peer cell: the same emitter gap on the closure-returning path (EmitDispatchableClosureReturningMethodImplementation). Rare in consumer code, so dispositioned supported-low-priority: a red is reported in the grid (the grid's purpose is to REACH this Latent), not release-gating. Reached on sim+device.
Control: the same shared closure-RETURNING method dispatched through the OWNER existential reads its own populated vtable, so it must be green independent of the fan-out fix.

cells.reason: @autoclosure (RC-CLOSURE) is Explicitly Out of Scope in roadmap.md: a compile-time Swift feature with no shipping-framework consumer; revisit only if one needs it. No fixture by design.

cells.runtimeNote: Headline writeback-observability fix: inout now projects as `ref T` and the C# caller observes the Swift mutation.
Two inout params writing back independently.
Blittable frozen-struct inout: post-call MarshalFromSwift readback lands the mutated fields back in the C# `ref` var.
inout Int32 on a class with mixed @_cdecl/CallConvSwift methods — writeback observed through the @_cdecl wrapper.
inout Int on a generic struct parent, routed through static protocol dispatch with `ref nint` writeback.
inout Int on a generic Collection conformer declared in an extension block (selector-collision shape).

cells.reason: HasInoutWithAbiMismatch rejects non-frozen (resilient) struct inout: a resilient struct is read through a pointer (no fixed layout), so it cannot be marshalled as a blittable `ref T` stack buffer with write-back. The method is not emitted — there is no runtime surface by design. Architectural ABI limitation, same family as the inout ObjC-bridgeable rejection (roadmap: 'Inout ObjC-bridgeable reverse-dispatch keeps a dead vtable slot').

inout ObjC-bridgeable (URL/URLRequest/Decimal) is rejected by HasInoutWithAbiMismatch on the direct path (the {p}Ref/{p}Copy write-back mismatch does not compile) and routed to a fatalError trap stub on the reverse-dispatch path. Roadmap 'Inout ObjC-bridgeable reverse-dispatch keeps a dead vtable slot' deferred it as disproportionate to a cosmetic dead slot on a near-unreachable signature; no active repro. No consumable runtime surface by design.

cells.reason: A sync/async tuple return with a generic element on a generic-parent extension (AsyncGenericContainer<T>.fetchPair() async -> (T, Int32)) is intentionally suppressed by the generator: a @_silgen_name async wrapper on a generic-parent extension is a generic instance method that expects self + parent type metadata in implicit registers, while a fixed CallConvSwift P/Invoke can only pass them as trailing IntPtr args — an ABI mismatch that SIGSEGVs. The 'properly suppressed' invariant is asserted in Swift.Bindings.Unit.Tests (MemberValidationPipelineTests.ValidateMethodEmission_AsyncOnGenericParent_*). No runtime surface by design; the correct long-term fix is a generic-static-dispatch @_cdecl async bridge.
